## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater rotifer characterized by a tiny armored body, flattened lorica, retractable head region, and small posterior toes used for crawling or anchoring on surfaces. In Florida, Lecane leontina has been recorded in the state’s rotifer fauna and would most likely be encountered in freshwater microhabitats such as ponds, marshes, wetlands, ditches, and vegetated littoral zones, especially among algae, detritus, biofilm, and submerged plants. Like other Lecane rotifers, it feeds on bacteria, algae, and fine organic particles, helping recycle nutrients in freshwater food webs while serving as prey for small invertebrates and larval fishes.
